why: True for a mesh that owns its geometry, but when a cloneTransformNode clone still holds the shared geometry the removed mesh is disposed (addToScene throws) while its buffers stay alive, so 'its buffers are destroyed' fails.
The probe shows both halves (parent assignment leaves children empty and is skipped, setParent fills children, addToScene sets parent from children) and the source has no other path.
Probe shows creation and addToScene leave light.shadowGenerator and scene.shadowGenerators empty and that the shadow task iterates scene.lights' shadowGenerator only, matching shadow-task.ts.
The real shadow task skips a generator with no caster list even with a receiving mesh present and renders exactly the listed meshes once set.
Probe lists the frame-graph task names after each register call; registerScene adds no 'shadow' task and the shadow variant adds exactly one.

Holds for an unparented light, but the depth range starts at the light's world position, so a light parented under a node at y=50 with light.position (0,0,0) still keeps a caster at the origin in range.

Reassigning scene.fog after setFog is uploaded, but an in-place edit (scene.fog.start = 7) is not: the render task's scene-UBO cache compares the fog object by identity and skips the write while the camera is still.

The plain-write and setter behaviour holds, but the advice fails for a hemispheric light: setLightDiffuseColor writes light.diffuse, which a hemispheric light lacks, and throws TypeError, and no setter exists for specular, range, exponent or groundColor.
Correct order and coupling in general, but 'differ whenever x and y are both non-zero' is false at x = y = pi or x = 2pi, where both orders give the same rotation.

True for meshes already built at registration, but a new mesh given receiveShadows = true and added after registerSceneWithShadowSupport samples the shadow map without any rebuild (control without receiveShadows does not).
Probe shows the late setFog leaves the built shader fog-free until the rebuild, and a material swap after the late setFog also stayed fog-free in my test.
onBeforeRender unshifts and _update iterates the list in order, so the last registered runs first, as both probe paths show.
Probe removes a nested mesh/light subtree and checks lists, nulled parent links and untouched children arrays, matching removeChildren/detachParent in scene-remove.ts.
Probe shows the removed child stays in parent.children, is re-added (or throws for a disposed mesh) with its parent, and setParent(child, null) first prevents that.

Holds for the shape factories probed, but the mesh factories createLines/createLineSystem/createDashedLines assign a default line material and take a name option (createLines gives 'lines' with material set).
Probe shows a 16-entry buffer with lights past the 16th dropped and setMaxLights(20) taking effect for a light state built afterwards.
The matrix is swap-moved as stated, but per-instance colors are not moved, so after removeThinInstance(mesh, 0) the instance now at 0 carries the last matrix with the removed instance's color.
Probe checks names (with children), null parent, shared material, _gpu and the same thinInstances object, matching cloneMeshNode/cloneTransformNode.
Probe shows the value overwriting the whole subtree and a hidden light still counted and written into the lights uniform.
Probe and addToScene/removeFromScene code agree: a camera added always becomes scene.camera and removing the active one sets null with no fallback.
Lists do hold duplicates and each removal splices one entry, though the first removal already disposes the mesh, which then stays listed as disposed.
Uniform scaling leaves direction unchanged as probed, but non-uniform scaling does turn it (direction [1,-1,0] with scaling (1,3,1) no longer points at 45 degrees), so 'scaling does not' is false.
True for a mesh owning its geometry, but when a clone shares the geometry the re-added mesh ends _disposed with its buffers still alive, so 'destroyed buffers' fails.
The array is kept by reference and direct writes need a version bump, but flushThinInstances is not the only one: setThinInstanceCount (or any other thin-instance call) uploads the direct write too.

Not shown per scene: enableMirroredMeshes(sceneA) installs process-wide, marking a mirrored mesh of an un-enabled scene B, and a mesh authored with sign -1 (glTF) with negative determinant is not marked.
Probe drives lightAffectsMesh through each precedence case and the code matches the stated order exactly.
onBeforeRender returns void, the callback survives removeFromScene of its target, disposeScene empties _beforeRender, and splicing removes one, as probed.
_update passes fixedDeltaMs when it is positive and the real delta otherwise, and it is initialised to 0, as the probe shows.
Push invalidation on own and ancestor TRS or parent writes keeps worldMatrix current on read, as probed; I found no in-engine write that leaves it stale.
setThinInstanceCount returns early with no thinInstances and the four named helpers dereference thinInstances! and throw TypeError, as probed.
addThinInstance starts at capacity 16 and doubles into a new F32 array, so an old matrices reference goes stale, as probed.

Unlinking holds, but 'disposes the light's shadow generator' was not shown: after removeFromScene(light) and drained retirements its shadow textures and UBO are not destroyed (only its task state is retired, deferred).
The wrapped _renderShadowMap skips rendering and uploads darkness 1 when disabled and the generator's darkness when re-enabled, as probed.
computeDirectionalLightMatrix fits the caster bounds in light view space and pads 10% per side, and the probe measures exactly that.
disposeScene disposes synchronously each mesh it was the last owner of and leaves meshes held by another scene alone, as probed.

Disposal of an unadded mesh holds, but on a mesh held only by another scene removeFromScene is not a no-op: it sets parent to null (the mesh jumps in world space) and cascades to its children, disposing any held by no scene.
